newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC to state major currency misalignments sorted.
newsitem.headline: APEC to state major currency misalignments sorted.

text.p: Finance ministers of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will state that major currency misalignments, as noted by the Group of Seven (G7) nations, have been corrected, Japanese delegation officials said on Saturday.
They said such a reference would be the first of its kind to be adopted by the APEC finance ministers, gathered at a luxury resort hotel here for their fourth annual meeting.
"Asian economies are a large enough part of the world that there should be a common understanding on exchange rates," one official said.
Japanese officials said the reference in the finance ministers' communique, to be announced on Sunday, will endorse the G7 statement made in Berlin in February.
The G7 said that major misalignments in currencies noted at their meeting in April 1995 had been corrected and called for currency stability in the foreign exchange markets.
Three APEC members -- Japan, the United States and Canada -- belong to the G7, which also includes Britain, France, Italy and Germany.

The statement will also likely propose macroeconomic cooperation and a freer flow of capital among the members of APEC, which also include Australia, Brunei, China, Chile, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Thailand, the Philippines and South Korea.
